## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Duccarita Sutta* ("Bad Conduct", Iti 64) is the fifteenth discourse of the section of threes (Tikanipāta) in the *Itivuttaka* [SuttaCentral]. Framed by the standard opening formula of the collection, the discourse addresses the three kinds of bodily, verbal, and mental misconduct [SuttaCentral]. It culminates in verse teaching that a foolish person who fails to make good karma and accumulates extensive bad deeds is reborn, upon the dissolution of the body, directly into hell (*akatvā kusalaṁ kammaṁ katvānākusalaṁ bahuṁ, kāyassa bhedā duppañño nirayaṁ so 'papajjati*) [Cohen 2006].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral identify a direct passage-level parallel in another discourse of the *Itivuttaka*, the *Tapanīya Sutta* (Iti 30), as well as in the Chinese translation of the *Itivuttaka* (T 765.65 焦惱) [SuttaCentral]. Closely resembling parallels are found across early Buddhist verse corpora, including the *Dhammapada* (Dhp 140), the *Udānavarga* (UV 28, Uv Kg 28, UVS 28), the Gāndhārī *Dharmapada* (G-Dhp 201–223), the Chinese *Dharmapada* translations (T 210, T 212, T 213), and the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 5.174, AN 6.45) [SuttaCentral]. Computationally, DharmaNexus aligns the opening prose with the Chinese *Dīrgha Āgama* (T 1) and identifies substantial Pali-internal text reuse with 19 texts, most prominently the *Nettippakaraṇa* (*Sāsanapaṭṭhāna*, Ne 37), the immediately succeeding *Sucarita Sutta* (Iti 65), the *Apaṇṇaka Sutta* (MN 60), the *Atapanīya Sutta* (Iti 31), and several other discourses in the *Itivuttaka* [DharmaNexus].
